output.reason: Sudden, painless, persistent monocular vision loss two hours ago in a 55-year-old is a stroke-equivalent presentation (e.g., central retinal artery occlusion or retinal detachment) requiring immediate emergency assessment today.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Sudden painless loss of vision in one eye that has not returned can mean a blocked retinal artery (a stroke-equivalent) or a retinal detachment, and treatment is time-critical. Do not drive yourself — have someone take you, or call 911 if no one can. Call 911 immediately if you develop weakness, numbness, facial droop, or trouble speaking.
differential: Central retinal artery occlusion / retinal TIA (amaurosis)
